title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck writes out the axioms for a 'PD differential graded algebra' (A^*, d, J, γ). These are the structures that a divided-power de Rham complex carries, the subject of his 1976 IHÉS talk.

(1) A^* is a graded abelian group in degrees ≥ 0. It has an associative unital multiplication with A^iA^j ⊂ A^{i+j}. It is alternating: xy = (−1)^{ij}yx, and x^2 = 0 for x of odd degree.

(2) d is a differential of degree +1 with d^2 = 0, satisfying the Leibniz rule d(xy) = (dx)y + (−1)^{deg x} x dy.

(3) J is a graded ideal containing A^+ = Σ_{i>0} A^i. So J = J^0 + A^+, and the condition is just that J^0 is an ideal of A^0. J is then automatically stable under d, since dJ^0 ⊂ A^1 ⊂ J.

(4) γ is a system of divided powers on J satisfying three conditions:
- homogeneity: x ∈ A^i ⇒ x^{(α)} ∈ A^{αi};
- for x of odd degree, x^{(α)} = 0 when α ≥ 2;
- compatibility with d: d x^{(α)} = x^{(α−1)} dx.

He then asks how to make sense of x^{(α)} for non-homogeneous elements, i.e. elements of A^even + A^odd. He tests this in the truncation A^0 + A^1, where J = J^0 + A^1. Since y ∈ A^1 has y^2 = 0, the natural definition is (x+y)^{(α)} = x^{(α)} + x^{(α−1)}y. He checks the addition axiom (z+z')^{(α)} = Σ_{i+j=α} z^{(i)}z'^{(j)}.
- Left side: (x+x')^{(α)} + (x+x')^{(α−1)}(y+y').
- Right side: the same plus an extra term (x+x')^{(α−2)}·yy'.

He concludes 'OK si yy' = 0'. This holds when A^1·A^1 lands in a degree that has been truncated away, i.e. in A^0 ⊕ A^1 with A^2 = 0.

The page belongs to the setup of the PD de Rham complex and of PD structures on dg algebras. It is unrelated to the surrounding pages, which treat categories of graded modules M_N, truncation and localisation functors.
errors: The failure he finds is real and conceptual: inhomogeneous elements z = x+y, z' = x'+y' do not commute (zz' − z'z = 2yy'), so the binomial axiom cannot hold for them in general. The standard fix is to impose PD axioms only on homogeneous (even-degree) elements, as Cartan did. Grothendieck notices this implicitly via the 'yy' = 0' condition but does not state the fix on this page.
Some entries are garbled (e.g. 'A^1A^1 ⊂ A^0', 'Λ^2A^1 → A^0'). In an alternating graded algebra one should have A^1A^1 ⊂ A^2. Probably a transcription or slip issue.

ideas.what: Axioms of a commutative (alternating) dg algebra with divided powers on an ideal J ⊇ A^+, compatible with d via d x^{(α)} = x^{(α−1)}dx and with x^{(α)} = 0 for odd x
ideas.modern_name: PD differential graded algebra / PD-dga (as in crystalline cohomology and de Rham–Witt theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Cartan (Séminaire Cartan 1954–55, divided powers on strictly anticommutative graded algebras); Berthelot (Cohomologie cristalline, 1974) and Illusie (de Rham–Witt, 1979) for the dg/de Rham setting
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such; the 1976 IHÉS talk itself appears unpublished

ideas.what: Extending a PD structure on J^0 to J^0 ⊕ A^1 via (x+y)^{(α)} = x^{(α)} + x^{(α−1)}y, valid when A^1·A^1 = 0
ideas.modern_name: Extension of divided powers across a square-zero module (I ⊕ M with M^2 = 0)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard lemma (Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline, ch. I; Berthelot–Ogus, Notes on crystalline cohomology)

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard axioms for PD dg algebras plus a routine verification. The only point of interest is seeing Grothendieck test the axioms on inhomogeneous elements and hit the non-commutativity obstruction (the yy' term). This is well known, and nothing here goes beyond Cartan, Berthelot and Illusie.
transcription_corrections: 'A^0.A^1 ⊂ A^1, A^1A^1 ⊂ A^0[?]' — the image reads 'A^0.A^1 ⊂ A^1, A^1A^1 ⊂ A^2' (or a truncation thereof), consistent with grading.
'x_i ∈ A^i, i impair, y ∈ A ⇒ x^{(α)} = 0' is better read as 'x ∈ A^i, i impair, α ≥ 2 ⇒ x^{(α)} = 0'.
'Sous-groupe[?]' is the heading 'Sous-groupe J' (the PD ideal).
Top line: 'A^* . d J γ — plus' lists the data (A^*, d, J, γ) with arrows to the axiom groups below.
